classification.difficultyReason: Combine the alternate segment theorem with the angle sum of a triangle.

content.prompt: Find the value of $a$, $b$ and $c$ in these diagrams.

spec.description: Inscribed triangle with a horizontal tangent at its bottom vertex; external b label has a leader.
spec.mathematics: Upper-right angle 42 degrees; right tangent–chord angle 73 degrees; unknowns a, b and c occupy the source sectors.

answer.worked:
$a=73^\circ$ and $b=42^\circ$ by the alternate segment theorem.
$$\begin{aligned}c&=180^\circ-73^\circ-42^\circ\\c&=65^\circ\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Vertical tangent at the left triangle vertex; 26-degree angle has an external leader.
spec.mathematics: Lower-left interior angle 83 degrees and lower tangent–chord angle 26 degrees.

answer.worked:
$a=26^\circ$ and $b=83^\circ$ by the alternate segment theorem.
$$\begin{aligned}c&=180^\circ-26^\circ-83^\circ\\c&=71^\circ\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Inscribed triangle beneath a horizontal tangent at the top contact.
spec.mathematics: Left tangent–chord angle 65 degrees; lower-left interior angle 69 degrees.

answer.worked:
$a=69^\circ$ and $b=65^\circ$ by the alternate segment theorem.
$$\begin{aligned}c&=180^\circ-69^\circ-65^\circ\\c&=46^\circ\end{aligned}$$
